historical_growth.basis: USD / US GAAP restated series only: revenue FY2021 $8,308m, FY2022 $9,463m (FY2023 10-K), FY2023 $11,790m, FY2024 $14,048m, FY2025 $16,383m. GBP/IFRS rows (FY2015-FY2022 in the CSV) are not chained to USD rows.

owner_fcf_series.note: reported FCF less SBC less equity-award withholding taxes (FY2023 $190m+$0m; FY2024 $202m+$98m; FY2025 $260m+$123m); levered, post-interest

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case FY2026-FY2030 average revenue growth. Historical revenue CAGRs (20.1% 3-yr, 18.5% 4-yr) are heavily M&A-inflated (Sisal 2022, MaxBet 2023, Snai/NSX/Betnacional 2025) and the FY2023 GBP-IFRS to USD-US-GAAP basis break prevents a clean 5-year figure. Equity CAGR is negative and meaningless (impairments, debt-funded Boyd NCI buyout, buybacks). EPS CAGR undefined (GAAP losses in FY2023 and FY2025).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity (-5.1%/yr) and owner FCF (-59%/yr, levered and restructuring-dragged) diverge sharply from revenue (+20%/yr): reported growth has been bought with debt and absorbed by acquisition integration, interest and higher gaming taxes. Owner FCF CAGR is far below reported FCF CAGR because SBC plus withholding taxes grew from $190m to $383m while reported FCF fell.
historical_growth.notes: 5-year figures deliberately omitted: FY2020 is GBP/IFRS and converting it at a historical rate would mix currency, GAAP (IFRS 16 vs ASC 842, revenue presentation) and the Stars Group merger step-change.

scenario_narratives.base: FanDuel's 2026 is a deliberate reinvestment trough (US adjusted EBITDA guided -18% y/y, Q3 ~breakeven) layered on top of Illinois/New Jersey tax step-ups and the one-week NFL delay; management is trading margin for AMP growth into 2027. The base case takes that at face value: group adjusted margin recovers from 14.8% in FY26 to the FY25 level (17.4%) by FY28 and to 20% by FY32, with Phase 1/2 cost savings largely absorbing gaming-tax inflation rather than expanding margins. ~$500m of 2026 transaction/restructuring cash fades to a ~$150m/yr serial-acquirer run-rate. Revenue growth decelerates from 9% to 3% over ten years as US legalisation matures. Leverage falls from 4.3x toward the 2.0-2.5x target through cash generation, not equity issuance.
scenario_narratives.bull: The reinvestment works: AMPs and US sportsbook handle recover through the 2026-27 NFL season, iGaming legalises in more states, FanDuel Predicts becomes a real third product, and no further state tax hikes land, so Phase 2 savings drop through and group adjusted margin reaches 23.5% by FY33 (US >20%, International ~24%). Revenue compounds ~10% for three years before decelerating. Still short of the 2024 investor-day ambition ($5bn EBITDA by 2027).
scenario_narratives.bear: The US sportsbook weakness is structural: churn from unfavourable results does not reverse, the DraftKings duopoly stays promotional, prediction markets erode SGP margin, and a cadence of state tax hikes plus the UK tax rise cap group adjusted margin at ~15% permanently. Brazil-style regulatory reversals recur in newer markets. New leadership misexecutes. Against $10.5bn of net debt the equity becomes a thin residual -- this scenario is a leverage story, not just a growth story, and its per-share value shows why the bear weight is above the house default.

valuation_philosophy.summary: House owner-FCF basis: SBC plus equity-award withholding taxes fully expensed (2.3% of revenue gliding to 1.8%), transaction/restructuring/integration cash charged against adjusted EBITDA, share count held flat, NCI deducted once in the bridge, unlevered flows discounted at a 9% USD WACC built on the target capital structure, with company-defined net debt ($10.5bn, ex player funds and ex operating leases) deducted. The valuation is a levered-equity call on whether FanDuel's 2026 margin trough is cyclical reinvestment or a structural reset; the bear/bull spread is dominated by that question and by the fixed $10.5bn debt claim ahead of equity.
key_risks_to_valuation: Leverage: at 4.3x net debt/EBITDA, each 1pp of permanent group margin is worth roughly $2-3bn of equity value; the bear case is a thin levered residual
US state gaming-tax cadence (Illinois per-wager levy, New Jersey, possible copycats) and the UK iGaming tax rise sit inside EBITDA and are not fully offset by cost programs
Regulatory reversal risk shown by Brazil's September 2026 ban (~1% of revenue; congressional ratification pending)
US sportsbook customer churn since Q4-2025 and the DraftKings duopoly; prediction-market cannibalisation of SGP economics
Leadership transition risk: new Group CEO (1-Oct-2026), new FanDuel CEO (May-2026), interim CLO
Transaction/restructuring cash ($471m FY25, ~$500m FY26) is treated as fading to ~$150m/yr; if a serial-acquirer run-rate is higher the margin paths are overstated
Sports-results variance can move a year's EBITDA by hundreds of millions in either direction
FY2026 year-1 flows partly overlap the June-2026 net debt anchor (<$1/share)

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API for NYSE: FLUT (USD) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 73.50-255.26. The FLTR.L London line was delisted 2026-08-03 and its feed is frozen at the 2026-07-31 print; it was not used.
data_sources.financials: FLTR.L_Metrics.csv (core_metrics rebuilt 2026-10-10); FY2025 Form 10-K (adjusted-EBITDA reconciliation, cash flow statement, EPS note, cover share count); Q2-2026 earnings release (balance sheet 30-Jun-2026, net debt, leverage, updated FY2026 guidance table, H1 cash flow); FY2023/FY2024 10-Ks for the USD/US-GAAP restated FY2021-FY2022 revenue and adjusted EBITDA.
data_sources.qualitative: FLTR.L_Analysis.json (2026-10-10): FanDuel leadership, Brazil exit, FY2026 guidance cut, leverage, leadership transitions, state tax hikes, UK tax increase.

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K adjusted-EBITDA reconciliation: share-based compensation expense $260m (no company combined figure published), plus $123m taxes withheld and paid on employee share awards (financing line 'Repurchase of ordinary shares and taxes withheld' $1,123m less $1,000m repurchases). Summed per house method because Flutter publishes no combined figure; the overlap (withheld shares are part of the expensed grant) makes the charge slightly conservative.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing outflow $1,000m; a further $250m completed 11-May-2026 (2.4m shares). $1.37bn returned since the Q4-2024 program began. Buybacks are value-neutral in this model (SBC fully expensed, count held flat) and are the mechanism that funds the flat count; management has paused further returns to deleverage.
inputs.fx_note: Single-currency valuation. Flutter reports in USD under US GAAP (since FY2023; GBP/IFRS before that) and, after the full LSE delisting effective 2026-08-03, trades only on the NYSE as FLUT in USD. The FLTR.L Yahoo feed is frozen at its last London print (2026-07-31) and must not be used for price or FX. No GBP conversion is attempted anywhere in this file.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted ~175.0m: 175.3m ordinary shares outstanding at 16-Feb-2026 (FY2025 10-K cover), less 2.4m repurchased in H1-2026, plus ~2m dilutive awards (FY2024 diluted 180m vs basic 178m; FY2025 anti-dilutive because of the GAAP loss). Matches the 175m diluted weighted-average used in Q2-2026 adjusted EPS. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would double-charge it.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Company-defined net debt $10,480m at 30-Jun-2026 (Q2-2026 release): gross debt at principal (~$12,043m; balance-sheet carrying value $11,978m net of discounts/deferred financing) less available cash $1,563m. EXCLUDES $1,986m player-deposit cash (matched by player liabilities), $72m restricted cash, and $581m operating lease liabilities (lease cost is an operating expense inside adjusted EBITDA under US GAAP, so leases are charged in the flows, not the bridge). Leverage 4.3x LTM adjusted EBITDA.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD-built rate. 10y UST ~4.1% + 5.0% ERP x beta 1.3 (levered online gaming) = ~10.6% cost of equity; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.5% (FY2026 guided net interest ~$640m on ~$12bn gross debt = 5.3%), ~4.2% after tax. Weighted at the stated TARGET structure (2.0-2.5x leverage, ~25% debt) = 9.0%. The current market structure (46% debt after the share price fell ~63% from the Dec-2025 high) would give ~7.7%, but using a collapsed equity value to lower the discount rate rewards the collapse; the target structure is used. Same 9.0% in all three scenarios: risk is charged once, in the flows.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B) by accounting standard: US GAAP operating lease cost (~$55m/qtr operating cash flow) is an operating expense inside adjusted EBITDA, so it is already charged in the flows. Operating lease liabilities ($581m at 30-Jun-2026) are therefore excluded from net debt. D&A path uses D&A excluding acquired-intangible amortisation (FY2026 guide ~$730m), which contains no right-of-use amortisation, so EBIT for cash tax is not double-charged.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows kept 100% consolidated; non-controlling interests deducted ONCE in the equity bridge at 30-Jun-2026 carrying value: $228m NCI (Sisal minority, CME) + $377m redeemable NCI (MaxBet, Junglee, Betnacional; carried at redemption value) = $605m. NCI share of net income is small (FY2025 -$27m, FY2024 +$53m). Boyd's 5% FanDuel redeemable NCI was bought out for $1,620m in FY2025 and is no longer in the bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company; routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 1-2; adaptations file read for leases/NCI). FRESH BUILD -- no prior DCF, no Drivers file, no memory entry. FY0 = FY2025 (USD, US GAAP); year 1 = FY2026 built from the 5-Aug-2026 guidance midpoint less the ~$70m Q4 Brazil revenue / ~$20m EBITDA loss from the 25-Sep-2026 ban. CURRENCY/BASIS BREAK: FY2015-FY2022 rows in the Metrics CSV are GBP/IFRS; FY2023+ are USD/US GAAP. Historical growth below uses only the USD/US-GAAP restated series (FY2021-FY2025 from the FY2023/FY2024 10-Ks); no CAGR is computed across the boundary. EBITDA MARGIN PATHS ARE NET OF A RESTRUCTURING HAIRCUT: Flutter's adjusted EBITDA excludes transaction, restructuring and integration cash costs (FY2023 $224m, FY2024 $189m, FY2025 $471m, FY2026 guide ~$500m). These are real recurring cash costs for a serial acquirer, so each scenario's ebitda_margin_path = company-definition adjusted margin minus a haircut of 2.8% (FY26), 1.8%, 1.2%, 0.8%, then 0.6% (~$150m/yr run-rate) -- both figures are given in the narratives. OWNER FCF ANCHOR: last_fcf $24m = reported FCF $407m (OCF $1,184m less capex $777m; FY2025 10-K) less SBC incl. withholding taxes $383m. It is LEVERED (US GAAP OCF is after $531m interest paid) and dragged by ~$470m of transaction/restructuring cash and working-capital swings; the component build is unlevered pre-interest, so the FY2026 model FCF (~$0.67bn) is not comparable to it and net debt carries the financing cost. interest_income is left at 0: Flutter earned $73m but is 4.3x net-debt, so nothing is counted twice. MINOR TIMING: June-2026 net debt already embeds ~H1-2026 levered owner FCF (~$0.1bn) which is counted again inside year-1 FCF; <$1/share. Shares held flat; buybacks value-neutral. Guidance basis: sports results at expected margin, stated FX, consistent regulatory/tax framework.

bear.narrative: FY2026 at the bottom of guidance ($17.4bn) less Brazil: adjusted margin 14.3% less 2.8% = 11.5%. Company-definition adjusted margin path 14.3 / 14.5 / 15.0 flat (haircut as base) -- i.e. the 17.4% FY2025 group margin is never regained. Axes: the US sportsbook churn since Q4-2025 proves structural, the DraftKings duopoly stays promotional and Kalshi/Polymarket-style event contracts cannibalise SGP economics, so US segment margin settles ~10%; further copycat state tax hikes (after Illinois per-wager levy and NJ) and the UK iGaming tax keep International at ~21%; integration costs never fade below $150m/yr; new leadership (Group CEO, FanDuel CEO, CLO all changed in 2026) misexecutes the NFL-season reinvestment. Capex stays 4.3% as Phase 2 savings are consumed by product catch-up. Revenue growth low-single-digit after FY2027 as Brazil annualises and US market growth stays mid-single-digit. With $10.5bn of net debt the equity is a thin, levered residual in this path: terminal growth 2.0%, cap 12x FCF.

base.narrative: FY2026 = guidance midpoint $17.91bn / $2.655bn less Brazil Q4 ($70m / $20m): revenue $17.84bn (+8.9%), adjusted EBITDA $2.635bn = 14.8% margin, less 2.8% ($500m) transaction/restructuring = 12.0%. Company-definition adjusted margin path 14.8 / 16.8 / 17.7 / 18.5 / 19.0 / 19.5 / 20.0 thereafter; haircut 2.8 / 1.8 / 1.2 / 0.8 / 0.6 thereafter. US recovers from the 2026 reinvestment trough (US margin ~10% in FY26 vs 13.2% in FY25) toward high-teens by 2029 as the Illinois/NJ tax step-ups are absorbed; International holds 21-23% after the UK iGaming tax rise; Phase 1 (>$300m) and Phase 2 ($500m opex+capex by 2029) savings mostly offset tax and reinvestment rather than expanding margins beyond 20%. Growth: Brazil annualises as ~-1pp in FY27; US mid/high-single-digit market growth plus iGaming; International 5-10%. SBC 2.3% of revenue (FY25 actual 2.34%) gliding to 1.8% as withholding-tax cash falls with the share price. D&A ex acquired intangibles ~4.1% (FY26 guide $730m), capex 4.6% (FY26 guide $815m) easing to 4.0% with Phase 2. Cash tax 24% of EBIT rising to 25% (FY2025 cash tax $445m; UK 25%, Italy, Australia 30%, US now taxable; Pillar Two floor). WC capture 0: player funds are ring-fenced and FY2025 OCF showed no reliable growth tailwind.

bull.narrative: FY2026 lands near the top of guidance ($18.3bn after Brazil; early Q3 'ahead of expectations' on World Cup engagement and favourable results): adjusted margin 15.0% less 2.8% = 12.2%. Company-definition adjusted margin path 15.0 / 18.0 / 19.5 / 21.0 / 22.0 / 22.5 / 23.0 / 23.5 thereafter (same haircut as base). Axes: the H2-2026 FanDuel reinvestment (loyalty program, BetProtect+, pricing) rebuilds AMPs and US sportsbook margin returns to the 2025 trajectory (US segment >20% by 2029, still short of the 25%+ investor-day ambition); more states legalise iGaming; FanDuel Predicts scales beyond the $50m 2026 start; Phase 2 savings drop through to margin because no further state tax hikes land; Brazil ban is not ratified. Capex eases to 3.8% with the Phase 2 capex savings. Terminal growth 3.0%, cap 15x FCF.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: 4.3x net leverage while EBITDA is falling, three simultaneous C-suite changes in 2026, two guidance cuts in a year, and a demonstrated regulatory tail (Illinois per-wager levy, NJ, UK tax, Brazil outright ban) make the levered-residual downside a live path. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right at once (US margin recovery AND no further tax hikes AND Predicts scaling AND clean leadership handover). Base 50%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
